title: Protecting Business Opportunities for Veterans Act of 2019
official_summary:
Protecting Business Opportunities for Veterans Act of 2019

This bill applies certain small business subcontracting limitations to contracts that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) awards to a small business concern owned and controlled by a veteran or a veteran with a service-connected disability.

The VA may award such a contract only after obtaining a certification from the offeror that it will comply with such subcontracting limitations if awarded the contract. Such certification shall specify the applicable performance requirements and explicitly acknowledge that the certification is subject to criminal penalties for making false statements in any matter within the jurisdiction of the U.S. government.

The VA Director of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization and the VA Chief Acquisition Officer shall jointly monitor compliance and refer any violation or suspected violation to the VA Inspector General.

If the VA determines that a contract recipient did not act in good faith, such recipient shall be subject to any or all of the following: (1) referral to the VA Debarment and Suspension Committee, (2) a criminal fine, and (3) criminal prosecution.

The Inspector General shall report on (1) the number of referred violations and suspected violations; and (2) the disposition of such violations, including the number of small business concerns suspended or debarred from federal contracting or referred for Department of Justice prosecution.

summary.headline: This law applies small business subcontracting limits to certain VA contracts awarded to veteran-owned small businesses and adds penalties for false compliance certifications.
summary.what_it_does: The law applies certain small business subcontracting limits to contracts the Department of Veterans Affairs awards to veteran-owned small businesses, including those with service-connected disabilities. Before awarding such a contract, the VA must get a certification from the bidder promising to follow those limits, and the certification must warn that false statements are subject to criminal penalties. The VA's small business office and chief acquisition officer must jointly monitor compliance and send suspected violations to the VA Inspector General. If the VA finds a contractor did not act in good faith, it may refer the contractor for debarment, impose a criminal fine, or refer it for prosecution, and the Inspector General must report on these referrals and outcomes.

who_it_affects.group: Veteran-owned small businesses and small businesses with service-connected disabled veteran owners
who_it_affects.how: They are the businesses whose VA contracts are covered by the subcontracting limits and monitoring rules.

who_it_affects.group: Companies that bid on VA contracts
who_it_affects.how: They must certify in writing that they will follow the subcontracting limits and face possible criminal penalties, debarment, or fines if they do not act in good faith.

who_it_affects.group: Prime contractors that hire subcontractors on VA work
who_it_affects.how: They must limit how much of the contracted work they pass to other companies, as set by the applicable subcontracting rules.

who_it_affects.group: Department of Veterans Affairs contracting staff and Inspector General office
who_it_affects.how: They must monitor compliance, refer suspected violations, and the Inspector General must report on the number and outcome of referrals.
